name: Basilique Sainte-Anne-du-Congo
subtitle: Modernist cathedral sanctuary conceived during Free France rule with parabolic arches and emerald-green tiled roof.

facts.label: Roofing
facts.value: Emerald-green glazed ceramic tiles shaped like fish scales

facts.label: Symbolism
facts.value: Monument to Free France and fusion of modernist reinforced concrete with African tribal architecture

parts.text: An architectural masterpiece in the Poto-Poto district of Brazzaville, commissioned in 1943 by Governor General Félix Éboué as a sanctuary honoring Free France. Designed by visionary architect Roger Erell, the basilica fuses European modernist concrete engineering with Central African organic aesthetics: its monumental parabolic arches recall traditional African wicker huts, crowned by a sweeping roof clad in glistening emerald-green glazed tiles patterned like the scales of river fish, illuminated by stained glass capturing Congolese everyday life and spiritual motifs.
